chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Harun ibn Kharija, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Among the qualities of humility is that you greet the one you meet.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.التَّوَاضُعِ: Humility, modesty, lowering oneself in status

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about humility and greeting others?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise tradition from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), linking the physical act of initiating a greeting (salam) directly to the spiritual virtue of tawaddu' (humility). This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on social etiquette as a means of eradicating pride, where the lower-status individual proactively demonstrates respect to elevate the social bond. It serves as a practical application of the Quranic command to greet with peace, framing it not merely as politeness but as a core component of moral character.
